columns.description: First day of the represented reference year.
columns.name: period

columns.description: The provider's reporting-area code, which is ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 except for its own EL for Greece and UK for the United Kingdom, or an aggregate code such as EU27_2020.
columns.name: geo_code

columns.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code for the reporting country, or null for the provider's aggregates, which are not countries.
columns.name: iso3_code

columns.description: Whether the row is a reporting country or one of the provider's own aggregates; one of 'country' or 'aggregate'.
columns.name: geo_kind

columns.description: People who established usual residence in the reporting country during the year, counted regardless of citizenship; null where the provider publishes no value for that country and year.

columns.name: observation_flag

indicators.attribution: Source: Eurostat, immigration by age group, sex and citizenship (migr_imm1ctz).
indicators.definition: The provider's immigration count under Regulation (EC) No 862/2007: the action by which a person establishes usual residence in the territory of a member state for a period that is, or is expected to be, at least twelve months, having previously been usually resident elsewhere. The citizenship dimension is the provider's total, so the count includes returning nationals rather than foreign nationals only.
indicators.licence: Eurostat reuse policy under Commission Decision 2011/833/EU: reuse authorised for commercial and non-commercial purposes provided the source is acknowledged
indicators.source: Eurostat, immigration by age group, sex and citizenship (migr_imm1ctz), series A.TOTAL.COMPLET.TOTAL.NR.T

model.description: One row per reporting country and reference year, carrying the number of people who established their usual residence in that country during the year, regardless of their citizenship, together with the provider's own aggregate of its member states.
model.name: european_immigration_flows

questions.derivation: Select the provider's immigration count by reporting country and reference year.
questions.question: How many people arrived to live in a country in each year the provider covers?

questions.derivation: Read which country and year combinations carry a value, and which carry the provider's flag instead.
questions.question: For which countries and years does this provider publish an arrival count at all?

temporal.meaning: Each period is the first day of the calendar year the flow occurred in, from the provider's TIME_PERIOD. The grain is one row per period and geo_code. The panel is not rectangular and cannot be made so: reporting begins in different years for different countries, and the United Kingdom's series ends with its withdrawal from the European Union, so a consumer reaching a recent year must show it as unpublished rather than as zero or as an absent shape. The provider collects a reference year by 31 December of the following year and releases it in March of the year after that, and revises published years continuously as national statistical institutes restate them.

validations.description: There is exactly one observation for each reporting area and reference year.
validations.name: one-row-per-area-and-year

validations.description: Period, area code and area kind are never null, however sparse the counts are.
validations.name: required-identity-is-never-null

validations.description: Every area the provider classifies as a country maps to an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code, and only its aggregates do not.
validations.name: every-reporting-country-carries-an-iso3-code

validations.description: No two reporting areas map to the same alpha-3 code.
validations.name: an-iso3-code-identifies-one-reporting-area

validations.description: No year records a negative number of arrivals.
validations.name: counts-are-never-negative

validations.description: Where the provider publishes a value it is a whole number of people; an absent value stays null rather than becoming a zero.
validations.name: a-published-count-is-a-count-and-not-a-placeholder
